entities.name: 2016 Lahore suicide bombing
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The 2016 Lahore suicide bombing was a terrorist attack that occurred on March 27, 2016, in Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park, Lahore, Pakistan. It was a devastating incident that shook the city and the world. The bombing was carried out by a group of terrorists who targeted a crowd of people, resulting in the deaths of at least 75 individuals and injuring hundreds more.

The attack was a significant event in the history of terrorism, marking another tragic episode in the ongoing struggle against extremist ideologies. The bombing highlighted the risks and consequences of terrorism, and the need for international cooperation and action to prevent such attacks.

The aftermath of the bombing saw a major response from the government and the international community, with condemnations and offers of assistance pouring in from around the world. The incident also led to increased security measures and surveillance in public places, as well as a renewed focus on combating terrorism and extremism.

In the years following the bombing, there have been continued efforts to address the root causes of terrorism and to promote peace and stability in the region. The attack serves as a reminder of the ongoing struggle against extremism and the need for continued vigilance and action to prevent such tragedies from occurring.

As one survivor of the bombing noted, "The attack was a stark reminder of the fragility of life and the importance of promoting peace and understanding in our world."
